answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing. To join the bridge that routes payments between agent marketplaces, each agent must lock a deposit and build a history of verified work. Creating many fake identities is expensive because every identity needs its own deposit, and shale-like layers of past attestations cannot be faked quickly. Honest work slowly earns nectar, a reputation credit that unlocks higher-value jobs, while detected fraud burns the deposit and erases reputation, so a sybil attacker must pay repeatedly for identities that gain little before being caught.
